chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

When you are sick and desire overtakes you, then perhaps it is the discharge, but it comes with a weak coming, not having strength due to your illness, hour after hour, little by little, so perform ritual bath (ghusl) from it.

key_terms.لِمَكَانِ مَرَضِكَ: Due to the location/state of your illness

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ritual bath (ghusl) for a sick person experiencing weak, gradual seminal discharge?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, clarifies a nuanced fiqh ruling where illness-induced weakness causes seminal discharge to occur gradually rather than in a single forceful emission. Scholars emphasize that despite the diminished physical strength, the discharge retains its legal status as *mani*, thereby obligating the full ritual bath (*ghusl*) to restore ritual purity for prayer. This ruling underscores the principle that the cause of the discharge (illness) does not negate its effect on ritual state.
